papers.title: SpecKV: Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Compression-Aware Gamma Selection
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by using a small draft model to propose candidate tokens that a larger target model verifies. A critical hyperparameter in this process is the speculation length γ, which determines how many tokens the draft model proposes per step. Nearly all existing systems use a fixed γ (typically 4), yet empirical evidence suggests that the optimal value varies across task types and, crucially, depends on the compression level applied to the target model. In this paper, we present SpecKV, a lightweight adaptive controller that selects γ per speculation step using signals extracted from the draft model itself. We profile speculative decoding across 4 task categories, 4 speculation lengths, and 3 compression levels (FP16, INT8, NF4), collecting 5,112 step-level records with per-step acceptance rates, draft entropy, and draft confidence. We demonstrate that the optimal γ shifts across compression regimes and that draft model confidence and entropy are strong predictors of acceptance rate (correlation ≈ 0.56). SpecKV uses a small MLP trained on these signals to maximize expected tokens per speculation step, achieving a 56.0% improvement over the fixed-γ=4 baseline with only 0.34 ms overhead per decision (<0.5% of step time). The improvement is statistically significant (p < 0.001, paired bootstrap test). We release all profiling data, trained models, and notebooks as open-source artifacts.
papers.llm_reason: 直接解决 LLM 部署核心瓶颈（推理延迟），用轻量 MLP 自适应选择推测解码长度 γ，在压缩模型场景下实现 56% 推理加速。实验覆盖 4 类任务 × 4 种 γ × 3 种压缩级别共 5112 条记录，统计显著性 p<0.001，开销仅 0.34ms/step。工程落地路径清晰：任何使用推测解码的推理框架都可直接集成。

papers.title: EvoPoC: Automated Exploit Synthesis for DeFi Smart Contracts via Hierarchical Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Smart contract vulnerabilities in Decentralized Finance caused over billions of dollars losses every year, yet the security community faces a critical bottleneck: identifying a vulnerability is not the same as proving it is exploitable. We propose a knowledge-driven agentic system for end-to-end contract vulnerability detection and exploit synthesis. Our core insight is that exploit synthesis is not a code generation task but a structured reasoning problem that requires grounded knowledge of protocol semantics, failure root cause, and exploit primitives. The system organizes this knowledge into a Hierarchical Knowledge Graph (HKG) that serves as structured memory for LLM-guided multi-hop reasoning. Evaluated on 88 real-world DeFi attacks and 72 audited projects (2,573 contracts), the system achieves 98% recall and 0.9 F1-score in detection, and a 96.6% exploit success rate (ESR), reproducing 85 historical exploits and recovering over $116.2M revenue. It outperforms SOTA fuzzers by up to 5× in ESR and 300× in recoverable value.
papers.llm_reason: 通过层次知识图谱驱动的 LLM 多跳推理，实现 DeFi 合约漏洞自动利用合成。98% 召回率、96.6% 利用成功率，在 88 个真实攻击 + 72 个审计项目（2573 合约）上验证。发现 16 个确认的 0-day，追回 $116.2M。将漏洞验证从纯代码生成提升为结构化推理 + SMT 验证 + 资产模拟。对安全审计、CI/CD 集成有直接趋势价值。

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces
papers.abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents evolve from isolated tool users into coordinated teams, reinforcement learning (RL) must optimize not only individual actions but also how work is spawned, delegated, communicated, aggregated, and stopped. This paper studies RL for LLM-based multi-agent systems through orchestration traces: temporal interaction graphs whose events include sub-agent spawning, delegation, communication, tool use, return, aggregation, and stopping decisions. Using this lens, we identify three technical axes: reward design spanning eight families; credit signals attaching to eight units from token to team; and orchestration learning decomposing into five sub-decisions. We connect academic methods to public industrial evidence from Kimi Agent Swarm, OpenAI Codex, and Anthropic Claude Code. We release an 84-entry tagged paper pool, a 32-record exclusion log, and a minimal JSON schema for replayable orchestration traces.
papers.llm_reason: 提出编排轨迹视角，系统化 RL 在 LLM 多智能体系统中的奖励设计、信用分配与编排学习。提供 8 族奖励、8 级信用单元、5 个编排子决策的概念框架。连接 Kimi Agent Swarm、OpenAI Codex、Anthropic Claude Code 等工业实践。84 篇论文池 + 可回放 JSON schema 是可复用资产。对构建多智能体系统的团队有架构设计参考价值。

papers.title: FlexSQL: Flexible Exploration and Execution Make Better Text-to-SQL Agents
papers.abstract: Text-to-SQL over large analytical databases requires navigating complex schemas, resolving ambiguous queries, and grounding decisions in actual data. We present FlexSQL, a text-to-SQL agent whose core design principle is flexible database interaction: the agent can explore schema structure, inspect data values, and run verification queries at any point during reasoning. FlexSQL generates diverse execution plans to cover multiple query interpretations, implements each plan in either SQL or Python, and uses a two-tiered repair mechanism. On Spider2-Snow, using gpt-oss-120b, FlexSQL achieves a 65.4% score, outperforming strong open-source baselines that use stronger, larger models such as gpt-o3 and DeepSeek-R1. When integrated into Claude Code as skills, our approach yields over 10% relative improvement.
papers.llm_reason: 灵活数据库交互的 Text-to-SQL Agent，在 Spider2-Snow 上 65.4% 超越更大模型的基线。工程理念清晰：允许 Agent 在推理任意阶段探索 schema、检查数据、运行验证查询。双层级修复（代码级→计划级）是实用的错误恢复策略。集成到 Claude Code 后带来 >10% 相对提升。开源代码可用。对数据分析自动化、自然语言查询接口产品有参考价值。

papers.title: HAAS: A Policy-Aware Framework for Adaptive Task Allocation Between Humans and Artificial Intelligence Systems
papers.abstract: Deciding how to distribute work between humans and AI systems is a central challenge in organisational design. This paper presents Human-AI Adaptive Symbiosis (HAAS), an implemented framework for adaptive task allocation in software engineering and manufacturing. HAAS combines a rule-based expert system that enforces governance constraints before any learning occurs, and a contextual-bandit learner that selects among feasible collaboration modes from outcome feedback. Three empirical findings emerge. First, governance is not a binary switch but a tunable design variable. Second, in manufacturing, stronger governance can improve operational performance and reduce fatigue simultaneously. Third, no single governance setting dominates across all contexts; moderate governance becomes increasingly competitive as the learner accumulates experience.
papers.llm_reason: Human-AI 自适应任务分配框架，将治理从二值开关提升为可调设计变量。contextual-bandit + rule-based expert system 的耦合设计是工程实践中的可迁移模式。发现制造业中更强治理可同时提升性能和降低疲劳（反直觉）。五维认知审计 + 五模自治光谱对 AI Agent 的安全治理设计有借鉴意义。
